text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Streaming endpoint v2/stream experiencing elevated tail latency and stalls. p95=360ms (SLO 200ms), p99=1.2s (SLO 500ms). Streaming stall rate 3.6%. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streaming/stream-tail?panelId=9

rachel (eng-oncall): Acknowledged. I'll coordinate. Nikhil/Josh, please confirm whether this is infra or serving slowness. Paging infra and serving.

nikhil (infra): Checking cluster-east-1. I'm seeing a cluster-level increase in GPU corrected ECC counters on nodes in rack-e2. Three nodes show thermal fan ramping and throttle_count increments. Listing: gpu-node-11, gpu-node-42, gpu-node-83.

josh (serving): Request queue latency rising on v2-stream workers on east pool. KV hitrate unchanged. Batching latency per-worker spiked. Looks like worker slowdown.

elena (hw-eng): NVML snapshot on gpu-node-42:
```
GPU1: temp=92C, perf_state=P2, throttle_reasons=THERMAL|SW_POWER_CAP, corrected_ecc=78, uncorr_ecc=0
GPU0: temp=67C, corrected_ecc=2
```
We see corrected ECC clustering on GPU1. Opening HW ticket HW-9922.

martin (sre): We should isolate the affected GPUs before they cause broader p99 regressions. Plan: cordon nodes, drain streaming pods, route traffic away from east-1 heavy pool, enable quantized fallback model and CPU-fallback for <1k sessions.

josh (serving): Applying emergency routing: prefer pool-west-2, reduce per-worker concurrency to 6, enable model-fallback=quantized-v2-small. Pushing runtime change.

deploy-bot: config-change: v2/stream emergency-route-2026-03-15 applied by josh. Diff: concurrency=6, prefer=pwest2, model-fallback=quantized-v2-small.

lydia (support): Customers impacted: analytics-pro and chat-saas-uk show elevated latency/error spikes. I'm preparing comms.

rachel (eng-oncall): Nikhil, start quarantining nodes. Martin, coordinate canary test once traffic is shifted. Elena, please collect nvml logs and PCIe errors.

nikhil (infra): Running cordon/drain on gpu-node-42 and gpu-node-83: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-42 && kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` then label `hardware=quarantine`.

josh (serving): Also toggling aggressive kv-prefix caching and reducing default max_seq to 1500 for streaming sessions to cut per-token work.

martin (sre): Canary plan: run long stream session emulation (2500 tokens) against new route policy and verify no stalls and that resume behaves. Starting canary: `./tools/stream_canary --endpoint v2/stream --tokens 2500 --retries 2`.

incident-bot: NOTICE: PagerDuty alert acknowledged by rachel (eng-oncall).

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by rachel (eng-oncall). On-call rotation: rachel -> nikhil if escalated.

martin (sre): Canary run 1: succeeded, minor jitter at ~10s connect, no streaming stalls observed.

josh (serving): Metrics after mitigation: p95 ~170ms, p99 ~480ms, stall rate down to 0.9%. Improvements visible within 60s. Live: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streaming/live

lydia (support): Status update drafted: "We've detected elevated latency and transient stalls on streaming endpoints. We've applied traffic rerouting and mitigation knobs. Hardware replacement scheduled for affected GPUs. Customers may experience short reconnects; no data loss expected." Posting now.

elena (hw-eng): Forensics note: corrected ECC errors spike correlates with high power draw events when model batch size > 8. NVLINK errors minor but present. We'll capture telemetry across swap. Inventory check: spare GPU boards in region east-1 rack spares.

nikhil (infra): Quarantine labels applied and autoscaler exclusion set. Pods drained off the three nodes. I'll also run a cluster-wide query for nodes with corrected_ecc>50 in past 24h and create a list.

josh (serving): I also deployed a short-term token-rate limiter per-API-key to prevent sudden bursts: `rate_limit.tokens=200/s` for streaming routes.

martin (sre): Running cluster sweep script: `scripts/find_high_ecc --since 24h --threshold 50` -> found 5 nodes across east clusters, flagging. Adding a CG alert for rising corrected ECC trend.

lydia (support): Customer "AcmeAI" asks for ETA. I told them hardware swap window estimate 90-120 minutes and we will provide progress updates.

rachel (eng-oncall): Action items: 1) nodes quarantined (nikhil) 2) routing + fallback applied (josh) 3) canary smoke passed (martin) 4) HW ticket opened (elena HW-9922) 5) support notifications (lydia). Add follow-ups to INC-1842609999.

elena (hw-eng): Will be on the replacement. After board swap we'll watch corrected_ecc counters and temperature profile for 30 minutes before unquarantine. If corrected_ecc resets and temps stable (<75C under load), we rejoin.

josh (serving): Will maintain emergency routing for 20 minutes and then slowly shift 20% back every 5 minutes subject to p99 staying <550ms. Rollback plan: if p99>800ms or stall rate>2% revert to fallback models and keep nodes offline.

martin (sre): Added temporary alert: `streaming.p99 > 750ms for 2m -> page infra+serving`. Also added `ecc.corrected > 100 in 1h -> page hw-eng`.

lydia (support): Status page now shows: "Mitigations in place; partial recovery. Hardware replacement scheduled. Next update in 30 minutes."

rachel (eng-oncall): Good work. Please append any diagnostics to the incident ticket and include raw NVML exports. We'll form a postmortem with ECC trend analysis and model-batching correlation. Closing PD alert after 15m stability window. :thumbsup:

josh (serving): Note for postmortem: instrument per-worker GPU utilization broken down by batch size and sequence length; add per-node streaming concurrency heatmap.

elena (hw-eng): Also recommend adding NVML streaming export to our node metrics pipeline for easier correlation in future.

nikhil (infra): Drain logs excerpt:
```
I03 14:12:01.001] cordon node/gpu-node-42
I03 14:12:05.223] drain evicting pod v2-stream-worker-3
I03 14:12:29.876] pod evicted and rescheduled to pool-west-2
```

martin (sre): Canary final: 3 runs, all passed. p99 sustained below 520ms. Closing immediate mitigation.

rachel (eng-oncall): Incident contained. Hardware ticket HW-9922 created; replacement in progress. Support notified customers. Follow-up postmortem scheduled. If regressions occur reopen. Incident ID INC-1842609999.

lydia (support): Posting final customer note: "Issue contained, mitigations applied, hardware swap in progress. We'll update at completion or in 30 minutes."
